📌 Zcash sets July 28 hard fork to seal Orchard after critical bug 

⚠️ Zcash founder Zooko Wilcox has explained how the network’s July 28 Ironwood hard fork will address uncertainty around a critical flaw in the Orchard shielded pool. The upgrade will not identify or freeze individual counterfeit coins. Instead, it will seal the old pool and limit how much ZEC can leave. 

🔖 Ironwood, also known as NU6.3, is scheduled to activate at block 3,428,143 on July 28. The upgrade will retire the current Orchard pool and introduce a new shielded pool based on the corrected circuit. According to Zcash’s official Ironwood user update, users will no longer be able to send or receive ZEC inside the old Orchard pool after activation. Funds can leave only through the turnstile, which prevents more ZEC from exiting than legitimately entered.

⭐️ The Zcash team said it believes the flaw was “unlikely to have been exploited,” but users cannot independently prove no counterfeit ZEC was created. Ironwood aims to trap any excess value inside the old pool rather than allow it to enter wider circulation. Security researcher Taylor Hornby discovered the Orchard flaw on May 29 while auditing the shielded system. The bug could have allowed an attacker to create counterfeit ZEC inside Orchard without leaving an obvious public record.

The moment a pool goes live, its price can slightly differ from the prices on major centralized exchanges (CEX). Smart traders and automated bots, known as arbitrageurs, are constantly scanning for these tiny gaps. They buy where it’s cheap and sell where it’s dear.

This isn't theoretical volume. Even today, with only a handful of live pools on Gala Swap, millions of dollars in arbitrage volume are flowing through the platform daily. Every single one of those trades pays a fee to the liquidity provider (LP).

Real Volume, Real Fees (Not "Farm Token" Emissions)

This is what makes Gala Swap different. The yield isn't based on inflationary "farm token" emissions that you have to constantly race against.

The LP rewards on Gala Swap are generated by real trading activity—the essential work of keeping the DEX price in sync with the broader market. When you provide liquidity, you become the infrastructure that makes this flow possible, and you earn your share of the fees from that volume.

The Real Gold Rush: Expanding the Surface

The current volume is impressive, but here’s what’s truly exciting: the bottleneck isn't the demand from traders; it's the surface area available for the arbitrage engine to work across.

A few dozen pools can only capture a few dozen tokens' worth of flow. Imagine this same efficient arbitrage engine running across hundreds of pools that simply don't exist yet.

The Takeaway:

The traders are ready. The volume is real. The arbitrage engine is already running. What's missing is the liquidity to serve that volume and capture those fees across a much broader range of pairs.

☢️ Israel’s Nuclear Apocalypse™: 30 Years of “Any Minute Now”

Historical fact: since the early 1990s, Benjamin Netanyahu has been promising that Iran will get the bomb “within 3–5 years.” 

From his 1992 Knesset speech to his 1995 book, from the cartoon bomb at the UN to endless interviews, the deadline keeps rolling while reality stubbornly refuses to cooperate. 

Israeli assessments swing from “by the end of the year Iran will have enough uranium for one bomb” in 2020 to “after the 2025 strikes Tehran has been pushed back two to three years,” but Bibi’s script never changes: “very soon, any day now.”

Campaign fact: in June 2025, the US and Israel hit Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan. Trump stood in front of cameras and declared that Iran’s “nuclear sites are totally and completely destroyed,” that the threat was over — “obliteration” as official branding. 

Months later, US intel and media reports politely walked that back: the program as a whole survived, the clock was set back by months, maybe a year, and significant enriched stock and centrifuges were moved or hidden. 

Before long, familiar estimates reappeared: Iran is roughly 9–12 months from a weapon, if it chooses.

Today’s intel line is boringly precise: Iran hasn’t made a formal decision to build a bomb, but it has the technical ability to get there in less than a year, even after airstrikes. 

Netanyahu’s rhetoric lives in a different universe: it ignores three decades of missed “red lines” and insists that every new report means disaster is days away — until the next assessment pushes the bomb back to “a few more months.”

🇮🇷 “Mount Pickaxe” and the Engineering of Fear

After the June 2025 war, one thing became obvious: the “destroyed” sites were just the visible layer. According to satellite analysis and Western reporting, Iran has been moving thousands of centrifuges into tunnels under so‑called “Mount Pickaxe” near Natanz and hardening its program deeper into the Zagros rock. Israeli and Western estimates now say Tehran’s breakout time remains around 9–12 months. The capability exists; the political decision does not.

Netanyahu’s system doesn’t know what to do with that ambiguity. For 30‑plus years he has sold the same storyline: Iran is “on the verge,” “months away,” “approaching the point of no return.” 

Trump, by contrast, tried to declare the story over: “we reduced Iran’s nuclear project to zero, the threat is gone,” a marketing campaign to book the war as a clean win. 

A year later, Mount Pickaxe, missing enriched uranium and fresh intel estimates quietly resurrect the mantra: the program lives, the timeline is back.

The result is institutionalized paranoia. Israeli political discourse ping‑pongs between “we destroyed everything” and “we are one minute from annihilation.” Mount Pickaxe is not just an engineering project; it’s a metaphor. The real program is buried deep, adjusting and surviving. Netanyahu’s fear stays on the surface, feeding on a Schrödinger bomb that is always simultaneously “almost ready” and “just pulverized from the air.”

The Israeli “nuclear apocalypse” has become less a forecast and more a political operating system — one that outlives presidents, contradicts facts and still dictates policy.
